question: Should OpenClaw core own a public ordered, immutable configuration-layer mode despite the existing `$include` and host-side composition paths?
rationale: The branch introduces a durable CLI and runtime contract with distinct precedence, security-policy, reload, and mutation semantics; implementation review cannot determine whether that contract belongs in core without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the core mode
options.body: Approve the public mode after the write-owner defect is fixed, the branch is rebased, and fresh-install plus upgrade lifecycle proof is added.

options.title: Keep composition host-owned
options.body: Use existing `$include` or external materialization and avoid adding another core configuration contract.

options.title: Wait for the RFC
options.body: Pause implementation until https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/34 establishes the intended ownership, precedence, and lifecycle model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the core mode
recommendation.body: Approve the public mode after the write-owner defect is fixed, the branch is rebased, and fresh-install plus upgrade lifecycle proof is added.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans core configuration policy and Gateway lifecycle, areas with repeated recent integration history under this handle.
